### Helper Functions

```{r}
#### Translate
translate_DNA <- function(dna_data){
  clean_dna <- gsub("[^ACTG]", "", dna_data)
  DNA_strings <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(clean_dna)
  translations <- as.character(Biostrings::translate(DNA_strings))
  return(translations)
}

#### Trim CDR3
trim_CDR3 <- function(seq_vec){
  return(substr(seq_vec, 2, nchar(seq_vec)-1))
}
```

## Algorithm

1. Randomly select a junction_aa from the data frame
2. Subset all junction_aa values with the same length
3. Assign all of the junction_aa values with >= 50% edit distance to the first junction_aa's "group"
    * All other junction_aa values should be returned to the original dataset
4. Perform this again until all junction_aa's have a "group" assigned to them


```{r}
tmp <- read.csv("~/VHH/data/S1-M02-TRIM_atleast-1_db-pass.tsv", header = T, stringsAsFactors = F, sep = '\t')

tmp$junction_aa <- trim_CDR3(tmp$junction_aa)
```


Subset samples for speed.

```{r}
# set.seed(1)
# df <- tmp[sample(1:nrow(tmp), 10000),]
df <- tmp
# Create variable for subsetting equal length CDR3s
df$junction_aa_length <- nchar(df$junction_aa)
```


```{r}
threshold <- (2/5)*100
results <- data.frame()
  # Start with 1 for group name
  group <- 1

time_stamp_one <- Sys.time()
while (nrow(df) > 1){
  if (group %% 100 == 0) cat("Clustering group: ", group, '\n')
  
  ## Randomly select a CDR3
  set.seed(group)
  # Select a single observation from DF
  tmp_CDR3 <- df[sample(1:nrow(df), 1),]
  
  # Subset all CDR3's with the same length
  tmp_frame <- df[df$junction_aa_length == tmp_CDR3$junction_aa_length,]
  
  # Calculate distances
  tmp_frame$distance <- stringdist::stringdist(tmp_CDR3$junction_aa,
                                               tmp_frame$junction_aa, 
                                               method = "lv")
  
  tmp_frame$distance <- 100 - (tmp_frame$distance/tmp_frame$junction_aa_length)*100
  
  # Drop any with less than the threshold
  tmp_frame <- tmp_frame[tmp_frame$distance >= threshold,]
  # Assign group
  tmp_frame$family <- rep(group, each = nrow(tmp_frame))
  # Increment counter
  group <- group + 1
  # Add to results
  results <- rbind(results, tmp_frame)
  
  # Remove tmp_frame data from df
  df <- df[!(df$sequence_id %in% tmp_frame$sequence_id),]
}
cat("Clustering took:\n")
print(Sys.time() - time_stamp_one)
```

```
2938 groups
Time difference of 11.6637 mins
```

```{r}
S1 <- results
```

This one time'd out and had many distinct duplicates in the `results`. Was it because there was a singlet left `(nrow(df) >= 1`?

**Because it kept going, it randomly selected clones and expanded out the families, but some families remained very underrepresented. Interesting.**

```{r}
S3 <- results
S3 <- S3[!duplicated(S3$sequence_id),]
```
